findings.title: Exit criteria and mode set diverge from the slice plan entry
The replacement performance gate does not show the 88% regression was recovered
findings.description:
The gate compares two modes that both scan every candidate in the neighbourhood (~1400 per agent at operational density, per line 19) over the same coherent fields. They differ only in the accept/accumulate block, so `k_nearest ≥ 0.8 × radius_only` can pass while both are far slower than today's `k_first` default.

- The only absolute anchor is 213.9 TPS at N=10k, and it applies to `radius_only`, not to `k_nearest` and not at 200k (line 357).
- Passing the gate flips the production default to `k_nearest` (line 197), so the live server from slice 146 could lose most of its throughput with every criterion green.
- The parent architecture's target is 60 TPS per tier, with Tier 3 at 250k. The design calls 200k "the architecture's Tier 3 target" (line 17) and restates no absolute TPS figure.

Add an absolute criterion: record the pre-change `k_first` TPS at N=200k on the dev CUDA box before the kernel rewrite, and gate `k_nearest` against that number as the plan specifies. Also restate the tier TPS target this slice is meant to move toward.

findings.title: `k_first` removal sequence contradicts itself
findings.description:
Three statements about `k_first` disagree:
- **Scope item 7 and lines 199 and 349:** `k_first` is removed entirely and raises `ConfigurationError`, with "no silent migration".
- **Mitigation, line 433:** the modes ship "alongside the legacy `k_first` value (still parsed, with a deprecation warning)" until the final commit.
- **Development step 2, line 442, and the AFTER sketch, lines 283-312:** the kernel is rewritten to two modes with no `k_first` branch, while `k_first` remains the default until step 4.

Between steps 2 and 4 the default value therefore has no kernel branch, and the design does not say what a `k_first` config executes in that window. Mapping it silently to another mode would violate the project's no-silent-fallback rule.

Other inconsistencies in the same area:
- Line 93 says no file outside the GPU compute path is touched, yet lines 349 and 452 edit `migratory_server/config.py`, `bench/workload.py` and the workload registry.
- Step 4 marks the plan entry `[x]` before the step 5 visual check, which is criterion 5.
- Line 165 calls the writebacks coalesced; line 461 says they "scatter".

State one sequence, specifying when the kernel branch, the parse acceptance and the default each change.

findings.title: Uncapped (`max_neighbors <= 0`) behaviour under `k_nearest` is unspecified
findings.description:
Slice 150 requires that agents with `max_neighbors <= 0` take the accept-all-within-radius path inside the kernel, and that `max_neighbors > MAX_K_HEAP` is capped with a warning. Item 8 "promotes" the uncapped sub-branch to `radius_only`, and the AFTER sketch's `k_nearest` branch has no uncapped case. With `max_neighbors == 0`, `heap_size < max_neighbors` is never true and the `elif` reads an empty heap root.

`max_neighbors` is per-profile and `neighbor_mode` is global, so a mixed population cannot be expressed by switching mode. The design must say whether the per-agent uncapped sub-branch is retained under `k_nearest` or whether `k_nearest` with `max_neighbors <= 0` becomes a configuration error. Parity criterion 2 does not cover this case.

findings.title: Coalescing premise depends on outer-loop order, and that risk is not listed
findings.description:
The design keeps the outer loop in original (spawn) order and rejects the coherent-order outer loop. Threads in a warp are then agents adjacent in spawn order, which are not spatially adjacent in general, so they walk different cell ranges of the coherent fields. Each thread gets sequential reads, but the cross-warp coalescing claimed at lines 17, 21 and 169 ("adjacent agents' heaps tend to evict slots from the same nearby cell range") does not follow.

The Hoetzlein reference the design cites iterates in sorted order. The rejection weighs four scattered writes per agent against roughly 1400 reads per agent, and the same document describes an O(N) scatter as cheap for the reindex (line 138).

This is my reading of the design, not a measured result, but the Risk Assessment omits it and the gate failure analysis (line 395) names only the inverse-permutation lookup and heap eviction. Add it as a risk, with the coherent-order outer loop as the named fallback if the 200k measurement falls short.

findings.title: Overweight relative to an Effort 3/5 slice; reference-chasing content can be cut
findings.description:
The reindex itself is small: seven fields, one kernel and an index substitution. Much of the document's weight comes from the 16M-boid reference comparison, which appears in six places: Overview, Reference points, Technical Decisions (lines 181-193), criteria 3 and 4, walkthrough step 5, and Future Work.

What to cut or defer:
- **"Reference points" section (lines 36-44)** and the repeated FRNN follow-up rationale. One Future Work bullet is enough.
- **Headroom probe (walkthrough step 5, lines 397-402).** It needs `mid-flock-500k` and `mid-flock-1M` workloads the scope never adds (only `mid-flock-200k`, line 452). It is not a gate, and it targets Tier 4 scale on a dev-class box.
- **`radius_only` at N=200k and N=1M (criterion 3).** The walkthrough only runs it at 10k.
- **`radius_only` as a shipped config mode,** if the plan is not amended (first finding). A bench-only measurement path meets the stated "speed reference" purpose.

findings.title: Dependency status and branch name
findings.description:
- Line 81 says slice 150 is "shipped on `main` as of 2026-05-05". The plan shows (150) unchecked and its slice document is `status: in_progress`. Slice 150's criterion (≤20% regression vs first-k) appears to be unmet given the 88% figure, so this design should say what state it actually depends on.
- Line 439 names the branch `152-coherent-grid-for-k-nearest-neighbor-search`. The project convention is the slice document name without `.md`, i.e. `152-slice.coherent-grid-for-k-nearest-neighbor-search`.
- Line 451 says spawn/despawn re-runs `setup()` and reallocates. Slice 146 describes a `from_numpy()` re-upload on count change. Either way the coherent fields stay correct because the originals are canonical, but the wording should match 146.
